title: The bundled hygiene tests use only the standard library and pytest, pass ruff, and pass where init set things up
assertion: Each of SWERepo's four hygiene rule tests (privacy, adr-index, changelog, ci-tests), as SWERepo renders them for `seamspec propose`, imports only the Python standard library and pytest, passes `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` with this repository's settings, and, run alone with pytest (no conftest) from `.seamspec/tests/` of a git repository that `swerepo init --yes` set up and committed, passes: on that layout as `init` left it, and with its security policy moved to `.github/SECURITY.md` holding a contact address. Each exits with failures, run alone, on the breakage it guards: a home-folder path in a tracked file, an ADR left out of the index, a changelog without `[Unreleased]`, `ci-ok` no longer needing `test`, `test`'s pytest step allowed to fail (`continue-on-error: true`), masked (`|| true`) or masked across a folded `run: >` block, `ci-ok`'s step that judges the jobs' results replaced with `echo ok`, and `ci-ok` no longer running `if: always()`.

origin.text: ADR-20261124-cd64 point 5 and spec §6.8: the hygiene rule tests run in the target repository, so they use only the standard library and pytest, ship ruff-clean (a locked test can't be tidied afterwards), and pass on what init sets up. Step-level and policy-path cases from Gemini's Phase 7 review (P7-F04, P7-F05); exit codes, each file alone, the unmodified layout, the folded block, and ci-ok still failing when a job fails after SeamSpec's reviewer.
